jobs.title: Geospatial Analyst, Senior
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

With cloud-based tools, faster GPUs, and the explosion of connected devices, geospatial data has more potential than ever. A skilled geospatial and remote sensing analyst can turn that data into mission critical information. If that sounds like you, we have an opportunity for you!

As a geospatial and remote sensing analyst at Booz Allen, you’ll work with a team of analysts to extract meaning and context from a variety of data sources. Using resources like SOCET GXP and iSpy, you’ll develop new ways to find patterns and connections to answer our Army's needs.

On our team, you’ll also use your skills to leverage satellite and airborne remote sensing solutions, and you’ll analyze data to assess meaning and potential intent. You’ll analyze and provide geospatial solutions for priorities like infrastructure, topography, human geography, and intelligence. Your geospatial skills will come in handy as you produce formal reports to make sure decision-makers have the have the timely information they need.

Work with us as we turn data into knowledge to support our warfighters and protect our national security.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have

Experience with geographically-derived assessments, enterprise data integration, spatial data governance, metadata management, and interpretation of business and performance metrics
Experience in coordination and collaboration with industry counterparts on technical projects, software and service assessment, and subject material
Experience using and managing spatial relational databases, including Oracle, MSSQL, PostGreSQL, or PostGIS
Experience with DoD or NSG Structured Observation Management (SOM) and object- based production
Knowledge of industry standard location analysis desktop and server applications, such as Esri ArcGIS Platform, QGIS, MapBox, or GeoServer
Ability to present geospatial information via multimedia presentations and written reports
Ability to work rotating shifts
Active TS/SCI clearance; willingness to take a polygraph exam
HS diploma or GED and 15+ years of experience with geospatial analysis or geospatial information systems, Bachelor's degree in a Geomatics or Geospatial Sciences field and 10+ years of experience in geospatial analysis or geospatial information system, or Master's degree in a Geomatics or Geospatial Sciences field and 5+ years of experience in geospatial analysis or geospatial information systems
Completion of a military service granting Imagery Analysis course, including MOS, AFSC, NOS or civilian equivalent

Nice If You Have

Experience with Intelligence Community (IC) and DoD geospatial data and repositories
Experience working within common project management frameworks
Experience using Python, R, SAS, Java, or other coding languages to deliver custom solutions
Experience with Army, DoD, or IC geospatial processes, policy, and programs
Experience in cartography, GIS, and spatial modeling
Knowledge of Microsoft Office tools and graphic design principles
TS/SCI clearance with a polygraph
Private Sector or Government Professional GIS Certification
Completion of an Army 35/350G, 12Y/125D, or 35F/350F Military Occupational Course

Clearance

Applicants selected will be subject to a security investigation and may need to meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information; TS/SCI clearance is required.

Our offerings include health, life, disability, financial, and retirement benefits, as well as paid leave, professional development, tuition assistance, work-life programs, and dependent care. Our recognition awards program acknowledges employees for exceptional performance and superior demonstration of our values. Full-time and part-time employees working at least 20 hours a week on a regular basis are eligible to participate in Booz Allen’s benefit programs. Individuals that do not meet the threshold are only eligible for select offerings, not inclusive of health benefits. We encourage you to learn more about our total benefits by visiting the Resource page on our Careers site and reviewing Our Employee Benefits page.

Salary at Booz Allen is determined by various factors, including but not limited to location, the individual’s particular combination of education, knowledge, skills, competencies, and experience, as well as contract-specific affordability and organizational requirements. The projected compensation range for this position is $77,500.00 to $176,000.00 (annualized USD). The estimate displayed represents the typical salary range for this position and is just one component of Booz Allen’s total compensation package for employees. This posting will close within 90 days from the Posting Date.

As part of the hiring process, we will ask you to complete an identity verification process that leverages advanced biometrics and artificial intelligence to ensure authenticity and protect against identity fraud. You are expected to be on camera during interviews and assessments. We reserve the right to take your picture to verify your identity and prevent fraud.

jobs.title: PhD: Modelling Impacts of Agricultural Practices on Soil Ecosystem Services
jobs.description:
Your job

The Earth Systems and Global Change Group at Wageningen University and Research invites applications for a PhD position (4 years) in a challenging project titled: “Modelling impacts of agricultural practices on soil ecosystem services across Europe”.

Preserving and restoring agricultural sustainability in Europe requires a monitoring framework quantifying how single and combined agricultural management practices affect European soil ecosystem services. The project aims to develop site specific recommendations for the implementation of agricultural practices in arable farming systems that enhance their contribution to a sustainable environment. The project is part of an ongoing European research project with 17 research partners. By finetuning and extending existing regional soil health assessment frameworks to assess the integrative contribution of crop, soil, nutrient and water management practices, this project will deliver new knowledge to enable farmers and policy makers to improve the ecosystem services the soil supplies, and to enable decision-makers to explore scenario outcomes, assess impacts and incorporate the results into soil quality related policy recommendations at national and EU level.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

As a PhD researcher, you will expand and improve an existing modelling framework to assess carbon and nutrient flows, and soil functions contributing to multiple ecosystem services, and the impact of management measures on regional level, assembling empirical and process-based algorithms considering agronomic and environmental impacts. You contribute to the following activities:

Develop a model to simulate and upscale impact of the combinations of farming practices on soil ecosystem services for regional / EU level
Perform an integrated spatial assessment of soil ecosystem services and adoption of farming practices, identifying synergies and trade off among arable farming practices in view of multiple ecosystem services
Assess the impact of co-created adoption policies / measurement packages at farm system level

You will work here

The research is embedded within the chair Earth Systems and Global Change Group (https://www.wur.nl/en/research-results/chair-groups/environmental-sciences/earth-systems-and-global-change-group.htm), which is led by Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-hhe-hannah-van-zanten) and Prof. dr. Nynke Hofstra (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-n-nynke-hofstra). You will be supervised by Dr. Gerard Ros (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/drir-gh-gerard-ros), Dr. Mengru Wang (https://www.wur.nl/nl/personen/dr-m-mengru-wang) and Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-hhe-hannah-van-zanten) from Wageningen University, and Prof Dr. Erik Meers from Ghent University.

Your qualities

You Are/have The Following

knowledge of soil health, nutrient and/or agrochemical cycles in agriculture;
experience in quantitative modeling and programming (e.g., R, python);
excellent scientific writing skills in English;
experience with publishing peer-reviewed academic journals is appreciated;
good organizational and intercultural communication skills;
willingness to travel across Europe.

You also possess:

a successfully completed MSc degree in environmental sciences, agricultural studies, or similar with a strong quantitative background;
enthusiasm for collaborating with an interdisciplinary team of researchers with diverse backgrounds and disciplines.
the entry requirements of the WUR PhD programme;
enthusiasm to do a PhD project at Wageningen University for four years.

For this position your command of the English language is expected to be at C1 level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale). Sometimes it is necessary to submit an internationally recognised Certificate of Proficiency in the English Language. More information can be found here (https://www.wur.nl/en/education/phd-programme/admission-requirements).

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

Partially paid parental leave;
working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8.3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will receive a fully funded PhD position and you will be offered a course program tailored to your needs and the research team.

The gross salary for the first year is € 3,204,- per month rising to € 4,051,- in the fourth year in according to the Collective Labour Agreements for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU) (https://www.universiteitenvannederland.nl/en/collective-labour-agreement-of-dutch-universities) (scale P). This is based on a full-time working week of 38 hours. We offer a temporary contract for 18 months which will be extended for the duration of the project if you perform well.

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, in an international and open working environment.

Coming from abroad

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/) can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account, dual career programs or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact Dr Gerard Ros via email: gerard.ros@wur.nl (mailto:gerard.ros@wur.nl)

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Jessa Rozema, Corporate Recruiter, via jessa.rozema-stol@wur.nl

Ready to apply?

To apply, please send the following documents ( max. 3 pages in total
):

Complete and up-to-date curriculum vitae (max. 2 pages);
Motivation letter (max. 1 page).

The maximum length of the documents must not exceed 3 pages. If it exceeds, applications will not be considered. Additional files such as grades and transcripts are not required during this stage and will not be considered.

The future of ONT starts now.
Through the ONT BOLD (Building Our Legacy & Destiny) Program, you can be a part of one of Southern California’s most ambitious airport development programs. ONT BOLD is transforming Ontario International Airport with a new terminal, modernized facilities, and infrastructure improvements designed to support future growth—and we’re looking for visionary leaders to help make it happen.

COMPENSATION

$135,000 - $195,000 annual salary + a generous benefits package to include medical, dental, vision and 10% employer paid 401A through VOYA Financial.
*Hiring Salary Range: $135,000 - $165,000 annual salary
(starting salary will be within this range based upon qualifications)

SUMMARY

The Airport Director of Planning and Environmental is responsible for leading the strategic planning, environmental planning, environmental compliance, sustainability, and airport development functions within the Capital Development Division. This position provides direction, oversight, and management of the Airport Planning and Environmental Department and serves as the Authority's subject matter expert on aviation planning, environmental regulations, and long-range airport development. Reporting to the Vice President of Capital Development, the Director oversees the planning and implementation of the Airport Capital Improvement Program (CIP), airport planning initiatives including ONT
BOLD
(Building our Legacy and Destiny), environmental review processes, and regulatory compliance activities while ensuring alignment with the Ontario International Airport Authority's (OIAA) Strategic Plan, Board priorities, and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Important and essential duties may include, but are not limited to the following:
Direct, manage, and oversee all airport planning, development, environmental planning, environmental compliance, and sustainability programs.
Lead the development, implementation, and periodic update of the Airport Capital Improvement Program (CIP), Airport Layout Plan (ALP), and other short- and long-range planning documents.
Direct, manage and coordinate the preparation of complex planning and environmental studies for the development and improvement of airport properties and facilities.
Oversee environmental planning and other system planning projects to ensure compliance with applicable Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) design standards, operating requirements, federal, state and local policies and regulations.
Establish planning priorities that support airport growth, operational efficiency, customer experience, and long-term infrastructure investment, and align with OIAA's Strategic Plan, ONT BOLD initiatives, Board directives, and aviation industry best practices.
Evaluate proposed airport development projects to ensure consistency with approved planning documents, operational requirements, and future development objectives.
Ensure airport development projects comply with FAA design standards, Advisory Circulars, engineering criteria, airport design requirements, and approved planning documents.
Oversee planning analyses related to airfield development, terminal expansion, landside improvements, utilities, transportation systems, and airport support facilities.
Plan and prioritize capital projects; develops and manages project budgets, implementation schedules, and stakeholder coordination during implementation.
Direct the preparation of federal, state, and local grant applications for funding; develops and oversees implementation of FAA infrastructure grants.
Direct and manage revisions to, as required, the Airport Layout Plan (ALP) to reflect as-constructed conditions and changes to future development plans.
Provide oversight of environmental permitting, mitigation monitoring, sustainability initiatives, and environmental compliance programs.
Lead environmental planning efforts that support responsible airport growth while balancing operational, community, and environmental considerations.
Review and monitor airport development projects for compliance with FAA requirements and environmental regulations, including but not limited to, the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) and all other local, state and federal regulations.
Work across Departments and Divisions to facilitate various planning and environmental activities to ensure efficient coordination of projects including scope, schedule, budget, and resources to ensure the ongoing development of the airport will meet the priorities set by leadership and the OIAA Board.

Your job

The Earth Systems and Global Change Group at Wageningen University and Research invites applications for a PhD position (4 years) in a challenging project titled: “Modelling impacts of agricultural practices on soil ecosystem services across Europe”.

Preserving and restoring agricultural sustainability in Europe requires a monitoring framework quantifying how single and combined agricultural management practices affect European soil ecosystem services. The project aims to develop site specific recommendations for the implementation of agricultural practices in arable farming systems that enhance their contribution to a sustainable environment. The project is part of an ongoing European research project with 17 research partners. By finetuning and extending existing regional soil health assessment frameworks to assess the integrative contribution of crop, soil, nutrient and water management practices, this project will deliver new knowledge to enable farmers and policy makers to improve the ecosystem services the soil supplies, and to enable decision-makers to explore scenario outcomes, assess impacts and incorporate the results into soil quality related policy recommendations at national and EU level.

Your Duties And Responsibilities Include

As a PhD researcher, you will expand and improve an existing modelling framework to assess carbon and nutrient flows, and soil functions contributing to multiple ecosystem services, and the impact of management measures on regional level, assembling empirical and process-based algorithms considering agronomic and environmental impacts. You contribute to the following activities:

Develop a model to simulate and upscale impact of the combinations of farming practices on soil ecosystem services for regional / EU level
Perform an integrated spatial assessment of soil ecosystem services and adoption of farming practices, identifying synergies and trade off among arable farming practices in view of multiple ecosystem services
Assess the impact of co-created adoption policies / measurement packages at farm system level

You will work here

The research is embedded within the chair Earth Systems and Global Change Group (https://www.wur.nl/en/research-results/chair-groups/environmental-sciences/earth-systems-and-global-change-group.htm), which is led by Prof. dr. Hannah van Zanten (https://www.wur.nl/en/persons/profdrir-hhe-hannah-van-zanten) from Wageningen University, and Prof Dr. Erik Meers from Ghent University.

About The Role

Muon seeks a Senior Technical Program Manager (TPM) to lead earth observation programs for U.S. Government customers. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of payload engineering and rapid-cycle space vehicle development. These programs span the full mission lifecycle — concept development and design through integration, launch, and on-orbit operations — and are executed under formal government contract structures with defined deliverables and milestones. The Senior TPM runs the program end to end: executing every contractual commitment and positioning Muon to win the work that follows.

The Senior TPM holds single-point accountability for delivering the program on schedule, within budget, and to technical performance standards. Operating with high autonomy on an accelerated contractual schedule, you will drive key milestones and lead cross-functional technical exchanges spanning systems engineering, payload, flight software, ground segment, and mission operations.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Responsibilities

Program Execution

Serve as the single accountable owner for the program's cost, schedule, and technical baselines
Own the integrated master schedule, cost baseline, and risk register; track and report progress against contract milestones
Plan and run formal program events — internal readiness reviews, and customer-facing milestone deliverable reviews
Maintain tight cost and schedule discipline; surface deviations to the customer promptly and with a recovery plan

Customer Interface

Act as the primary programmatic interface to the Government customer, including contracting and technical representatives
Lead technical exchange meetings and convert customer input into actionable program direction
Own the delivery and quality of all contract data deliverables

Cross-Functional Leadership

Direct a cross-functional team spanning systems engineering, payload, flight software, ground processing, and mission operations
Partner with mission operations when program activities involve Muon's operational systems — without disrupting existing missions
Drive design trades and study conclusions to closure on schedule, escalating crisply when decisions stall

Security, Compliance, and Growth

Execute the program in full compliance with its government security requirements, including handling of controlled information and strict public-release restrictions
Ensure compliance with ITAR/EAR export controls and U.S.-only performance requirements
Support program growth: convert program artifacts into proposal-ready material and support capture of follow-on opportunities

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in engineering or a technical field, or equivalent experience.
8+ years of program management experience on complex aerospace or defense development programs, including direct ownership of cost, schedule, and technical baselines
Experience executing U.S. Government contracts: statement-of-work and CDRL deliverables, milestone-based structures, and day-to-day work with government contracting and technical representatives
Experience leading engineering teams through concept development, trade studies, and preliminary design
Exceptional written communication skills — you will author and own the quality of customer-facing reports, design artifacts, and contract deliverables

Preferred Qualifications

Satellite or instrument program leadership across the full lifecycle (design, build,
integrate, test, operate)
Domain experience with remote sensing systems — EO/IR, RF, or both — at the payload or mission level
Direct experience working with USSF Space Systems Command or JPL
PMP certification or equivalent program management credentials
Ability to obtain a security clearance

Salary

The salary range for this role is $206,000 - $232,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

new_jobs.title: Director of Planning & Environmental
new_jobs.description:
The future of ONT starts now.
Through the ONT BOLD (Building Our Legacy & Destiny) Program, you can be a part of one of Southern California’s most ambitious airport development programs. ONT BOLD is transforming Ontario International Airport with a new terminal, modernized facilities, and infrastructure improvements designed to support future growth—and we’re looking for visionary leaders to help make it happen.

COMPENSATION

$135,000 - $195,000 annual salary + a generous benefits package to include medical, dental, vision and 10% employer paid 401A through VOYA Financial.
*Hiring Salary Range: $135,000 - $165,000 annual salary
(starting salary will be within this range based upon qualifications)

SUMMARY

The Airport Director of Planning and Environmental is responsible for leading the strategic planning, environmental planning, environmental compliance, sustainability, and airport development functions within the Capital Development Division. This position provides direction, oversight, and management of the Airport Planning and Environmental Department and serves as the Authority's subject matter expert on aviation planning, environmental regulations, and long-range airport development. Reporting to the Vice President of Capital Development, the Director oversees the planning and implementation of the Airport Capital Improvement Program (CIP), airport planning initiatives including ONT
BOLD
(Building our Legacy and Destiny), environmental review processes, and regulatory compliance activities while ensuring alignment with the Ontario International Airport Authority's (OIAA) Strategic Plan, Board priorities, and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) requirements.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

Important and essential duties may include, but are not limited to the following:
Direct, manage, and oversee all airport planning, development, environmental planning, environmental compliance, and sustainability programs.
Lead the development, implementation, and periodic update of the Airport Capital Improvement Program (CIP), Airport Layout Plan (ALP), and other short- and long-range planning documents.
Direct, manage and coordinate the preparation of complex planning and environmental studies for the development and improvement of airport properties and facilities.
Oversee environmental planning and other system planning projects to ensure compliance with applicable Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) design standards, operating requirements, federal, state and local policies and regulations.
Establish planning priorities that support airport growth, operational efficiency, customer experience, and long-term infrastructure investment, and align with OIAA's Strategic Plan, ONT BOLD initiatives, Board directives, and aviation industry best practices.
Evaluate proposed airport development projects to ensure consistency with approved planning documents, operational requirements, and future development objectives.
Ensure airport development projects comply with FAA design standards, Advisory Circulars, engineering criteria, airport design requirements, and approved planning documents.
Oversee planning analyses related to airfield development, terminal expansion, landside improvements, utilities, transportation systems, and airport support facilities.
Plan and prioritize capital projects; develops and manages project budgets, implementation schedules, and stakeholder coordination during implementation.
Direct the preparation of federal, state, and local grant applications for funding; develops and oversees implementation of FAA infrastructure grants.
Direct and manage revisions to, as required, the Airport Layout Plan (ALP) to reflect as-constructed conditions and changes to future development plans.
Provide oversight of environmental permitting, mitigation monitoring, sustainability initiatives, and environmental compliance programs.
Lead environmental planning efforts that support responsible airport growth while balancing operational, community, and environmental considerations.
Review and monitor airport development projects for compliance with FAA requirements and environmental regulations, including but not limited to, the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) and the National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA) and all other local, state and federal regulations.
Work across Departments and Divisions to facilitate various planning and environmental activities to ensure efficient coordination of projects including scope, schedule, budget, and resources to ensure the ongoing development of the airport will meet the priorities set by leadership and the OIAA Board.
Direct the preparation of Professional Services Agreements, technical specifications and plans for various studies and technical services; recommends and approves contract awards; and organizes, coordinates and supervises the work of consultants.
Represent and serve as the OIAA representative on local, regional and/or national organizations regarding planning and environmental technical issues.
Lead and direct the activities of assigned staff; reviews work plans; meets with staff to identify and resolve problems; assigns work activities and projects; monitors workflow; evaluates employee performance and work products.
Communicate airport planning and environmental objectives, goals and progress to OIAA senior management and stakeholders.
Meet with officials of public and private agencies, community groups, and individuals to explain aviation development related issues; effectively communicates with internal and external stakeholders on technical subject matter expertise.
Direct, plan, manage and coordinate the development and implementation of goals, objectives, policies, and priorities; establishes, within OIAA policy, appropriate service and staffing levels; allocates resources accordingly.
Does related work as required.
May occasionally be assigned to other duties for training purposes, technological changes or deficiencies or for emergency response.
Required to visit project sites at terminal, airside or landside locations. Attendance at off-site meetings for presentations, networking and other industry events also required.

PROFILE OF THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

Extensive experience leading airport planning and environmental programs at a commercial service airport or similarly complex aviation organization.
Comprehensive knowledge of airport planning principles, airport master planning, capital improvement programming, transportation planning, and aviation infrastructure development.
Thorough understanding of FAA regulations, Advisory Circulars, Orders, Airport Improvement Program (AIP) requirements, and airport planning guidance.
Extensive knowledge of environmental planning and regulatory compliance, including NEPA, CEQA, permitting requirements, environmental documentation, and sustainability initiatives.
Knowledge of federal, state, and local grant administration, funding programs, and reimbursement requirements.
Experience developing long-range strategic plans and implementing complex capital development programs.
Strong project and program management skills with the ability to manage multiple high-profile initiatives simultaneously.
Experience leading multidisciplinary teams and managing consultants, technical professionals, and cross-functional project teams.
Demonstrated success developing departmental budgets, strategic priorities, performance objectives, and organizational policies.
Strong political acumen and the ability to effectively navigate complex governmental, regulatory, and stakeholder environments.
Excellent leadership, coaching, mentoring, and employee development skills.
Exceptional written, verbal, presentation, and negotiation skills.
Strong analytical, organizational, and decision-making abilities with sound professional judgment.
Ability to effectively communicate complex technical information to executive leadership, elected officials, regulatory agencies, community organizations, and the public.
Ability to establish and maintain productive working relationships with employees, tenants, airlines, consultants, contractors, governmental agencies, and community stakeholders.
Knowledge of current and emerging technologies affecting airport planning, infrastructure development, environmental compliance, and asset management.
Familiarity with airport operations, airline requirements, aviation industry trends, and the communities served by Ontario International Airport.
Ability to consistently model and demonstrate the Ontario International Airport Authority's Core Values through ethical leadership, accountability, innovation, collaboration, and exceptional public service.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education, training, and experience that would likely provide the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform in the position.
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Airport Planning, Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Environmental or a related field is required. A Master's degree in a related field is highly desirable.
Eight (8) years of progressively responsible and recent professional experience or consultant work, in aviation planning projects and programs, preferably at a FAA Part 139 Certified Airport, including a minimum of three (3) years in a lead or supervisory capacity.
Experience at a commercial airport and working with an appointed board or elected officials is highly desirable.
Familiarity with and work experience in the Southern California region is a plus.
Experience with CEQA preferred.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and database programs.

LICENSES / CERTIFICATION

Valid Driver's License equivalent to a California Class C Driver's License
Acceptable driving record at time of appointment and throughout employment
Ability to pass all background / reference checks, knowledge examinations, as well as aptitude tests necessary to obtain an OIAA employee badge at ONT
